title: Clarification on what is allowed when using tools, specifically TKoolBridge.

posts.author: bubblezzzzzz
posts.body:
I would like to know if it is legal to use TKoolBridge with RPGMaker 2000.
TkoolBridge
is a tool that converts event commands created with the RPG Maker 2000 event editor into text code format. It also has the ability to automatically generate event commands by editing the code.
Thank you.
It is considered freeware, so there isn't any issue on the creator side, just unsure if it violates any RPG maker rules.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
While I cannot say specifically if it is in breach of the license, I can give you a general rule of thumb:
If it directly decompiles/modifies the editor itself, it is likely against TOS.
That said, it sounds like it only extracts information, in which case likely is not modifying the editor.
Maybe others can provide a more clear answer.
You can also try googling this specific tool and see if there are any existing discussions on its legality.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
This tool does not modify RPG_RT.exe or the editor, it only allows you to edit commands and events in the clipboard, from what I understand, the tool itself was suggested in another topic, even so it is good to wait for a response:
AkiraKotatsuhime said:
The change-command is made to set new types of screenblend for when a teleport, battle-entrance or battle-end will occur. Use hide and show instead, they are on page 2, last entries on left side, see image in post #3.
View attachment 218404
If you plan to change player's position too while you are at it, you have to use the change-command to remove the teleport's fadeout and set it back to default afterwards. The player's position-change by transfering has to be the last of position-changing steps, because the screen will show when it finishes.
View attachment 218406
Just add temporary changes to show-screen if the default one is not what you plan to use.
With help of TKoolBridge, TKcodeScripter or MEX, you can also use the set-vehicle-location command to reference the player instead of a vehicle.

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
It just parses clipboard data and doesn't modify anything RM-side at all so my personal opinion would be that it's fine, even with RM2k.
(With RM2k3 it would be even less of a concern by the way because it has a patch EULA.)
